deep.reconstruction:
The page continues the 'Remarques' begun on p.51. There Grothendieck showed that for f: X→S smooth (proper, or quasi-projective), the de Rham complex Rf_*(Ω•_{X/S}) carries a canonical absolute connection (Gauss–Manin), in the derived-category sense. He then speculates that these connections might come from canonical stratifications, that is, from compatible Taylor-type isomorphisms p_1^*E ≅ p_2^*E over all infinitesimal neighbourhoods of the diagonal (equivalently, a crystal structure in the naive non-PD sense).

This page says such a canonical stratification would give an 'a priori' explanation of the invariance in Washnitzer–Monsky theory. Concretely, MW cohomology does not depend on the choice of dagger lift, and close maps induce the same map on cohomology. That would follow from a stratification transporting the cohomology of one lift to another along 'infinitesimally close' morphisms.

He then corrects himself:
- In characteristic 0 this is true, since an integrable connection is the same as a stratification.
- In characteristic p>0 it is false. Take the structural projection of a family of elliptic curves (an elliptic scheme). The Gauss–Manin connection on H^1_dR has nonzero p-curvature when the family is non-isotrivial, so it cannot come from a stratification, which forces p-curvature 0.

The link between stratifications and MW invariance is therefore called a 'heuristic and sentimental relation' between two ideas whose exact relationship remains far from elucidated.

He sums up the situation as a 'puzzle': build a global theory combining three ingredients.
- (a) A cohomology theory of complexes of differential operators, aimed at de Rham cohomology.
- (b) A systematic study of stratified structures, especially relative ones, with conceptual explanations.
- (c) Washnitzer–Monsky theory.

The next page (§4, stratifying and crystalline topoi) starts building the site-theoretic framework for (b).
errors: No mathematical error. The char-p counterexample is correct: the Gauss–Manin connection of a non-isotrivial family of elliptic curves has nonzero (nilpotent) p-curvature, as later made precise by Katz. A stratification would force p-curvature zero, so it cannot exist.
The phrase 'C'est bien vrai si S est de car. zéro' is fine. In char 0, integrable connections and stratifications coincide, at least for formally smooth S.

ideas.what: Gauss–Manin connections might come from canonical stratifications. This fails in char p, with elliptic families as the counterexample.
ideas.modern_name: Stratification vs connection; p-curvature of the Gauss–Manin connection; the need for PD-stratifications (crystals)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (crystals, 1966–68); Berthelot (crystalline cohomology); Katz (p-curvature of Gauss–Manin, 1970)
ideas.where_published: 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (IHES notes 1966, in Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas, 1968) discusses stratifications vs connections and the char-p failure

ideas.what: Heuristic: a stratification would explain the independence of Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology from choices of lifts.
ideas.modern_name: Overconvergent stratifications / overconvergent isocrystals; rigid cohomology
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in the Crystals notes; not developed there

ideas.what: Programme: unify (a) cohomology of complexes of differential operators, (b) stratified structures and crystals, (c) Monsky–Washnitzer theory.
ideas.modern_name: Berthelot's arithmetic D-modules (D^†) and rigid cohomology unifying MW and crystalline cohomology
ideas.where_published: unsure; the 1966 Crystals notes mention differential operators and crystals but not this explicit three-part programme with MW

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly frames Monsky–Washnitzer invariance as a stratification phenomenon. He sets as a programme the unification of differential-operator cohomology, stratifications/crystals, and MW theory. This anticipates Berthelot's rigid cohomology and arithmetic D^†-modules, where the 'missing' stratification is the overconvergent one: Taylor series converge on strict neighbourhoods of tubes. This programme was later carried out, so it is not truly missed. The page is, however, an early documented articulation of it by Grothendieck, which is not usually cited.
missed.quote: Pour résumer, on se trouve conduit devant un puzzle, où il s'agit de reconstituer une théorie d'ensemble combinant a) Une théorie cohomologique des complexes d'opérateurs différentiels ... b) Une étude systématique des structures stratifiées ... c) La théorie de Washnitzer – Monsky.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical credit: it shows Grothendieck foresaw the synthesis realized by Berthelot (rigid cohomology plus arithmetic D-modules) around 1967. Mathematically the thread has been taken up.

deep.surprise_reason: The ideas, including the char-p failure via elliptic families, are consistent with the Crystals notes and were later fully developed by Katz and Berthelot. The explicit three-part 'puzzle' linking MW theory to stratifications and differential operators is a nice early statement of the rigid/arithmetic D-module programme, but it is not a new result.
